chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Ḥumayd ibn Ziyād, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad al-Kindī, from more than one narrator, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the palm-stalk placed in the grave. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: If a woman miscarries, and the fetus is complete at four months or more, it is to be given ghusl, shrouded, and buried. But if it is less than four months, it is wrapped in a cloth and buried in its blood without ghusl.

key_terms.الْجَرِيدَةِ: the palm-stalk placed in the grave
key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: the grave in which the deceased is buried
key_terms.تَغْسِيلٍ: the act of washing the deceased
key_terms.خِرْقَةٍ: a piece of cloth in which the fetus is wrapped
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: it was given ghusl (ritual washing for the deceased)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on placing a palm-stalk in the grave and on burying a miscarried fetus in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report addresses burial-related rulings, stating that placing a palm-stalk in the grave is permissible. It also gives a legal ruling on a miscarried fetus: if it has reached four months or more, it is washed, shrouded, and buried; if less, it is wrapped and buried without ghusl.
